findings.problem: The new validator raises ValueError for user-editable values such as a non-http scheme, a link-local or metadata IP, or a malformed URL. It does this even for disabled instances. Pydantic turns that into a ValidationError, and nothing catches it. ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:370-373) only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError. Its docstring (config.py:344-345) says ValidationError is left to propagate because it means a schema bug. startup.py:192 calls ensure_config with no handler. So a hand-edited triggarr.toml with, for example, url = "radarr:7878" on a disabled instance used to load and now crashes the daemon at startup with an uncaught traceback through asyncio.run. It never reaches the friendly loguru error-and-exit path used for corrupt TOML. The rejection is intended (see the docstring). The problem is that the failure is unhandled.

findings.problem: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171) blocks only by exact match against BLOCKED_HOSTS and by ipaddress.ip_address parsing. Some host forms fail both checks and are accepted as ordinary hostnames, but the OS resolver used by httpx still maps them to the metadata address. Examples: http://2852039166/ (decimal for 169.254.169.254), http://0xa9fea9fe/, http://0251.254.169.254/, and http://metadata.google.internal./ (trailing dot). findings.title: Config-load SSRF check can be bypassed with numeric or trailing-dot host forms that resolve to cloud metadata (data exposure)
findings.why_it_matters: The docstring promises that metadata addresses are blocked at config load, but alternate spellings of the same address get through.

agent_notes: The diff itself is a pure tightening: before this change, triggarr/models/config.py had no SSRF validation at config-load time at all (confirmed via git log and .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-RESEARCH.md:295, which states 'No SSRF validation currently runs at config-load'). Loading triggarr.toml directly previously accepted any URL unconditionally; this diff now rejects cloud-metadata/link-local/non-http URLs at startup. That is a security improvement, not a regression.

The change matches its intent doc closely: .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-RESEARCH.md and 71-CONTEXT.md (decisions D-01/D-02) describe exactly this field_validator, exactly this relaxed-vs-strict split (web form stays strict at routes.py:561; config-load is relaxed to permit loopback/localhost), and the exact docstring wording used in the diff.

Not reported as a security finding but worth flagging to the engineer: because the validator now runs unconditionally on InstanceConfig.url (including disabled instances), any existing triggarr.toml with a non-compliant URL on a disabled instance (malformed, non-http scheme, or a blocked address) will now raise pydantic.ValidationError at Settings construction. triggarr/config.py:333-373 (ensure_config) does not catch pydantic.ValidationError -- only tomllib.TOMLDecodeError/UnicodeDecodeError and OSError are handled -- so this propagates uncaught and crashes app startup with a traceback to stderr/logs (not exposed to end users, since it happens before the web server starts). This is an intended/documented behavior per the D-01/D-02 design docs ('intended hardening'), but it is an availability/upgrade consideration rather than a vulnerability, which is why it isn't included as a finding above.

reject_apikey_in_url and validate_url_ssrf are both field_validator('url') on the same field with no mode= specified (default mode='after'); Pydantic v2 runs same-field validators in class-body definition order, so apikey rejection runs before SSRF validation as intended -- no ordering issue found.

findings.fix_hint: in validate_arr_url[_config], after the ipaddress.ip_address() ValueError branch, re-check the raw hostname string for a trailing dot / all-digit / 0x-prefixed form and reject or normalize before treating it as an opaque DNS name
findings.problem: The new field_validator wires InstanceConfig.url through triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config (unchanged in this diff; added in prior commit 14eecb5). That helper's hostname check does `ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)` and, on ValueError, falls through to 'treat as DNS hostname, no further check' -- the same pattern already used by the web-form validator validate_arr_url. Non-canonical IP literal encodings (trailing-dot 169.254.169.254., decimal-integer 2852039166, octal, hex) all raise ValueError from Python's strict ipaddress parser, so they bypass both the BLOCKED_HOSTS exact-string match and the ip_address()-based link-local/metadata checks. If the resolver used by the app's HTTP client (httpx, over glibc getaddrinfo in the likely Debian-based Docker image) accepts these forms as the literal address, a TOML-configured URL using one of these encodings could still reach 169.254.169.254 despite validate_arr_url_config rejecting the canonical form. This is a pre-existing gap in the shared helper's logic (also present in validate_arr_url for the web-form path since commit 1a8c9f9), not something introduced by this diff's own changed lines -- the diff only extends an already-imperfect validator to a new call site, and before this diff config-load had no SSRF validation at all, so this is a net improvement.
findings.title: New config-load SSRF validator inherits non-canonical IP literal bypass from shared helper
findings.why_it_matters: If the bypass is confirmed against the actual resolver in use, a homelab admin (or anyone who can write triggarr.toml) could configure a *arr URL that resolves to the cloud-metadata address or another blocked internal target despite the new validator appearing to reject it, defeating the SSRF hardening this diff is meant to add.

agent_notes: The codebase already has one non-web-to-web deferred import: triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538 lazily import from triggarr.web.routes. Lazy cross-layer imports are therefore tolerated precedent, which is why arch-001 is held at medium severity and confidence 50 rather than higher.
No import cycle is introduced: triggarr/web/validation.py imports only ipaddress, re and urllib.parse; triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, so importing it does not pull in FastAPI or routes.

Pattern consistency: the new validator follows the existing @field_validator('url') + @classmethod + raise ValueError convention set by reject_apikey_in_url in the same class. Stacking two field_validators on 'url' is valid Pydantic v2; they run in definition order, so the apikey check fires first. tests/test_config.py::test_instance_config_metadata_url_with_apikey_rejects_apikey_first appears to pin that order.

Duplication: validate_arr_url (strict, used by web/routes.py:561) and validate_arr_url_config (relaxed) are two near-duplicates in triggarr/web/validation.py. That is below the rule of three, so it is not a finding. If a third URL-policy variant shows up, extract a shared core with a parameter such as allow_loopback.

Defense-in-depth layering: routes.py validates with the strict validate_arr_url, then InstanceConfig construction applies the relaxed validator. Strict-at-UI plus relaxed-at-load is coherent, but the UI form will reject loopback URLs that a hand-edited TOML accepts. Confirm this asymmetry is intended (the D-02 docstring suggests it is).

Possible correctness item for the bugs lane, not architecture: reject_apikey_in_url short-circuits on an empty url, while validate_url_ssrf relies on validate_arr_url_config accepting '' (its docstring mentions '' for a disabled instance). Verify that '' returns (True, '') so default InstanceConfig() and disabled instances still load.

findings.fix_hint: Move the SSRF URL validators (validate_arr_url, validate_arr_url_config, BLOCKED_HOSTS, _BLOCKED_NETWORKS) to a layer-neutral module, e.g. triggarr/url_safety.py or triggarr/models/url_validation.py, and re-export from web/validation.py. Then use a top-level import in config.py.
findings.problem: Before this diff, triggarr/models/ was a leaf layer. models/config.py and models/arr.py import only stdlib, pydantic and pydantic_settings, while triggarr/web/routes.py and triggarr/web/middleware.py import models.config. The new validator reverses that direction: it imports triggarr.web.validation, the web UI's form-input helper module (its docstring says it is for 'the settings form'), into the config model that the scheduler, engine, db, state and startup modules all load. The function-local import is a sign the author expected a cycle risk. There is no actual cycle today, because validation.py imports only stdlib and web/__init__.py is empty, but nothing enforces that.
findings.title: Config model layer now depends on the web presentation package for URL validation
findings.why_it_matters: If anyone later adds an import of triggarr.models.config (or anything FastAPI-related) to web/validation.py or web/__init__.py, config loading will hit a circular import or pull web dependencies into every non-web consumer of the config model. The security-critical SSRF policy would also live under a package named for the UI.

agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is imported by 9 production modules and 17 test files. The new validator runs every time any Settings/SettingsModel is built: at startup (ensure_config -> load_settings), on the settings POST (routes.py:598), on add_instance (routes.py:793), and on the four load_settings reloads after a write (routes.py:1199/1462/1511/1535). The reloads only re-read config that was just validated, so the new check only fails them if the on-disk file was already bad.

No public API or signature change. The validator only adds new ValidationError cases. Every current call site that builds the model already catches pydantic.ValidationError (routes.py:599, routes.py:794) except startup, which is impact-1.

Settings-form interaction: the POST route runs the stricter validate_arr_url first (routes.py:561), which blocks loopback. The new config-level validator allows a strict superset of what the form allows, so no URL the UI accepts can be rejected by the model. The form still can't save a 127.0.0.1 or localhost URL that the config file now allows. That inconsistency already existed and is intended per D-02.
The 'preserve existing instances' branch (routes.py:582-594) copies existing URLs back through the model. Those URLs already passed validation at startup, so this branch can't be newly broken.

Tailscale CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) is only blocked for IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals. Plain 100.x.y.z IPv4 URLs pass (verified 'http://100.101.1.2:7878' -> True), so Tailscale-addressed *arr instances are unaffected.

No database, schema or migration changes. The v2.2->v2.3 migration (config.py:74) passes URLs through unchanged, so a migrated config with a now-rejected URL hits the same startup failure as impact-1.
Performance: negligible. The function-local import is a sys.modules lookup after the first call, and the validator is pure string/ipaddress parsing with no DNS lookups, run only when config is built.

Layering: models/config.py now imports from triggarr.web.validation inside the function, presumably to avoid an import cycle. validation.py imports only stdlib, so a top-level import would also work. This is style, not a defect.
Verification: the full suite passes (982 passed). tests/test_config.py already covers metadata-URL rejection, including for disabled instances.

Verdict: shippable as a hardening change. Before release, I recommend handling pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config with a friendly exit (impact-1) so upgraded users with hand-edited configs don't hit an unexplained crash loop.

findings.fix_hint: In ensure_config, catch pydantic.ValidationError and log a friendly, path-only error with no input values (like _log_corrupt_config_and_exit), naming the instance or field, then sys.exit(1). Add a release note that hand-edited URLs pointing to 0.0.0.0, link-local addresses, metadata hosts or non-http schemes are now refused at startup.
findings.problem: Before this diff, the config-file path never ran an SSRF check. URLs only went through validate_arr_url on the settings form (routes.py:561). Now validate_url_ssrf runs inside Settings(**data) at load_settings (config.py:226), called from ensure_config (config.py:371). ensure_config only turns TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError into a friendly message plus exit. Its docstring (config.py:345) says pydantic.ValidationError is a 'schema bug' and is left to propagate uncaught. That error is now an ordinary operator mistake. If a user edited the TOML by hand to use a URL the old code started fine with, the upgraded container dies at startup with an asyncio.run traceback and no hint about how to fix it. I checked these: http://0.0.0.0:7878 (on Linux, 0.0.0.0 reaches the local host, so this worked before) gives 'Blocked address'. A scheme-less 'localhost:7878' on a disabled instance gives 'URL scheme must be http or https'. Under Docker restart:unless-stopped this becomes a crash loop. Pydantic's ValidationError text also includes input_value=<url>, and it goes to stderr, not the loguru redacting sink. A URL with userinfo (http://user:pass@host) would print those credentials. Rejecting these values is the intended hardening (D-01/D-02). The defect is the failure handling on the new rejection path.

findings.why_it_matters: Every user who upgrades with an affected hand-edited TOML gets a service that won't start and a confusing traceback. The settings UI can't fix it because the app never comes up.
